Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. # - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the woman's jacket fully closed in the edited image, with no visible opening along its front closure?
node.criteria: Pass if the visible front closure shows the jacket fully closed, with its panels meeting and no opening along the closure. Fail if a visible opening along the closure shows that the jacket is open or partly closed. Unknown if the closure cannot be assessed because of pose, occlusion, or image quality; a panel hanging outward alone is not evidence of an opening.
node.binding: Assess the woman's jacket in the edited image against the requested fully closed state, using the source image as context for the requested change. Judge the visible front closure, not the direction in which a panel hangs. If the closure is not visible enough to determine whether it is closed, return unknown.

node_traces.evidence: In the edited image, the jacket’s front is visibly open: its panels are separated, with a dark gap along the front rather than meeting at the closure. The panel hanging outward is not the basis for this judgment; the visible opening is.

response.content: {"text":"The node’s criterion is appropriately tied to the requested fully closed state, and the trace is valid with no transport or dependency failure. The edited image does show a jacket panel hanging outward, but the trace asserts a visible dark gap at the front closure without clearly distinguishing that gap from the panel’s silhouette or the turned pose. Tighten the evidence test to locate the closure itself and verify that the gap is between the front edges; do not treat an outward-hanging panel alone as proof of an opening. Compare with the source only to establish the requested change, not as a substitute for assessing the edited closure. If the closure cannot be resolved in this view, return unknown rather than a confident fail. The reference label is aggregate guidance, not atomic ground truth, so investigate this evidence ambiguity rather than forcing a yes."}
